focus: hook budget GS6, mcp_tool transport, Node startup, parallel batches

findings.claim: GS6 budget (Claude Code mcp_tool hook p95 <= 40 ms wall; other agents <= 20 ms CPU over bare Node) can only be hit today by a Bun/Node fallback chain that the owner's own rule bans.
findings.evidence: TECH-SPEC.md:39 says bare Node alone is 45.6 ms p95 on the owner's Mac, close to or over the 40 ms wall budget. The real code that hooks use to hit this budget is resolveHookRuntime() in src/runtime.ts (added in commit 4c74a1bf, 'add resolveHookRuntime + buildHookRuntimeCommand for bun auto-detection (#738)'): it probes for a Bun binary and 'bun --version', and if that fails it uses a variable literally named `nodeFallback`. The comment on buildHookRuntimeCommand (src/adapters/types.ts:397-412) states this swap is what 'cuts ~40-60ms of Node cold-start per tool call' -- i.e. the 40ms wall budget is not met by Node alone, it is met only when the Bun path is taken. Owner decision list (relayed in this task) states a flat rule: 'no fallback chains'. try-Bun-else-Node is a fallback chain by definition.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY: 4c74a1bf 'feat(runtime): add resolveHookRuntime + buildHookRuntimeCommand for bun auto-detection (#738)', 2026-05-31, v1. ORIGINAL_INTENT (code comment, src/adapters/types.ts:401-403): 'Hooks run end-to-end in pure JS (no native modules) so swapping the runtime is a no-op for output but cuts ~40-60ms of Node cold-start per tool call.' REGRESSION_RISK: if v2 removes the Bun probe to comply with 'no fallback chains', GS6's 40ms wall number becomes unreachable on a plain Node host, since bare Node startup alone already costs 45.6ms p95 per the owner's own TECH-SPEC line. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: TECH-SPEC must either (a) name the Bun/Node switch as an explicit, documented exception to 'no fallback chains' with a stated reason (startup cost, not correctness), or (b) restate GS6 with a budget that is reachable on Node alone, or (c) require Bun as a hard dependency for Claude Code hook mode (removing the 'else Node' branch, so there is one named runtime, not a chain).
findings.fix: Either (a) add one sentence to TECH-SPEC/ADR-0008 or ADR-0010 naming the Bun-detect-else-Node runtime switch as the one explicit exception to the no-fallback-chain rule, with the cold-start number as the stated reason, or (b) change GS6 to a number bare Node can hit, or (c) make Bun a hard requirement for the <=40ms path and report 'budget not met' (not silently fall back) when Bun is absent.

findings.claim: #1261 ('Pre/PostToolUse hooks cost 55-70 ms CPU per Bash') is an open v1 issue with no fix commit in v1 history; TECH-SPEC's GS6/GP3 numbers are not shown to be reconciled against this measured 55-70ms figure.
findings.evidence: tickets/v2-issue-map.md:22: '1261 | Pre/PostToolUse hooks cost 55-70 ms CPU per Bash | ... | D7/D8: bundled TS hooks, no DB; matcher limited; PostToolUse async where host allows'. tickets/v2-issue-map.md:70: '#1261: D8 keeps PostToolUse on every tool call; per-call process cost stays unless hooks are async. Not a contradiction, but a perf budget is needed.' `git log --all --grep=1261` and `git log --all -S 1261` in the v1 history (cm-main) return no commit: the issue was never closed in v1. TECH-SPEC §6.5 GS6/G26 states a <=40ms p95 target and GP3 bench as the check, but does not show the 55-70ms measured CPU figure being retested or explained away; 'PostToolUse async where host allows' is a stated requirement, not a shown implementation for Claude Code (PostToolUse hook output is read synchronously by the host per the Claude Code hook contract, so 'async' needs a concrete mechanism, e.g. fire-and-forget spawn with detached stdio).
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY: issue #1261 has no fixing commit (search exhausted: git log --all -S/--grep '1261' on cm-main returns nothing past the doc commits). ORIGINAL_INTENT: n/a, never implemented. REGRESSION_RISK: if v2 keeps PostToolUse synchronous (as the current hook scripts in src/adapters/claude-code/hooks.ts do -- POST_TOOL_USE_MATCHERS fires posttooluse.mjs on every Bash/Read/Write/mcp__ call with no async flag in the matcher config), the 55-70ms per call cost from #1261 reproduces unchanged and GS6 cannot pass GP3 bench on CI hardware slower than 'the owner's Mac'. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: any fix must not add a fallback/retry path (owner rule) and must not write unindexed large output into the host log; async dispatch must still guarantee the index write completes before the next PreToolUse read depends on it (ordering, per #985/#1213 concurrency findings).
findings.fix: Add a line to TECH-SPEC/ADR naming the concrete async mechanism for PostToolUse on Claude Code (e.g. detached spawn + host does not wait on stdout), and add a GP3 case that replays the #1261 scenario (plain `ls`) and asserts PostToolUse wall/CPU under budget, not just a generic bench.

findings.claim: The 45.6 ms bare-Node p95 figure in TECH-SPEC.md:39 is stated as fact with no source command, script, or dataset named.
findings.evidence: The line reads '(bare Node alone is 45.6 ms p95 on the owner's Mac)' with no pointer to a benchmark script, raw data file, or GP3 fixture that produced it. No matching file was found under docs/v2/review/out or e2e/ in a non-exhaustive check.
findings.archaeology: n/a (no code change involved; this is a numeric claim, not a behavior).
findings.fix: Name the benchmark script/fixture that produced 45.6 ms (or add one under e2e/) so GP3 bench and GS6 can be re-run and re-verified instead of trusted as a one-off number.
